The *Ekacintikattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 189) is a Pali verse narrative included in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya, recounting the past-life meritorious deeds and spiritual attainments of the elder (thera) Ekacintika [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

These connections are confirmed by DharmaNexus text-reuse data, which demonstrates very substantial verse alignment between Tha-Ap 189 and Tha-Ap 329 (spanning segments §0.1–11.2 with 0.95 similarity), as well as significant shared text with Iti 83 (§0.3–6.4 aligned with Iti 83 §12.1–18.4 at 0.87 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies smaller shared formulaic verse sequences with the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Atthasandassakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 139, §11.3–13.1), and the *Ekacāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 191, §11.3–14.1) [DharmaNexus].
